_why: Status here is verified by `npm run gate`, not asserted by hand. A finding marked `fixed` must name either `checkedBy` (a static check id the gate already runs) or `verify` (a quote-free command the gate executes). If that check starts failing, the gate fails and this table is proven wrong â€” the entry cannot go quietly stale.

findings.title: serve bound every interface with auth off (RCE via npm postinstall)
Unauthenticated build API rendered any absolute local path
Attribute injection / XSS: escapeHtml did not escape quotes
resolveSite prefix-confusion read sibling sites
Subdomain `..` escaped the hosting dir; CLI --name was never slugified
findings.detail: Server-side slug guard landed in v3.7.0 (checkedBy inv-6). The CLI deploy path now always routes the requested name through combineSubdomain, so `brewdocs deploy --name ../x` slugifies to `x` instead of writing outside the hosting dir.

findings.title: emitRedirects wrote outside outDir via a `from: "../x"` key
findings.detail: Reachable from any repo's brewdocs.yml (`redirects:`). The `skip: file exists` guard prevented overwriting but not creating outside the output tree. emitAliasPages was checked at the same time: its alias name goes through dirSafe, which maps separators to `_`, so it could not traverse â€” but the write target is now confirmed inside outDir anyway.

findings.title: publish.yml publishes on any v* tag with no typecheck or smoke build
findings.detail: publish.yml ran only `npm ci` + `npm test`, so a tag on a commit whose types do not compile still published three packages. It now runs `npm run verify` (typecheck + map + gate + tests) plus a smoke build before any publish. Provenance attests where it was built, not that it works.

findings.title: @brewdocs/core ships raw TypeScript; plain Node cannot import it
findings.detail: Core shipped raw src/**/*.ts, so `import '@brewdocs/core'` under plain Node threw ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING. It now builds to dist (tsconfig.build.json, excluding tests), ships dist/ with a types+import exports map, and builds via prepublishOnly. Dev, tests and typecheck still resolve workspace source through tsconfig paths + a vitest alias, so the CLI keeps running TS directly (D-2).

findings.title: API key scopes are stored and printed but never enforced
findings.detail: keys.ts persisted and printed `scopes` but server.ts never read them, so a `--scope build` key performed every operation. Write endpoints now call authorize(req, scope) and return 403 when the key's scopes do not include build/export/markdown; the admin token still grants all, and a key with no scopes means all (keys.ts).

findings.title: Rate limiter trusts X-Forwarded-For unconditionally
findings.detail: clientKey() trusted X-Forwarded-For unconditionally, so rotating the header defeated the limiter. It now keys on the socket address unless the operator opts in via ProtectionOptions.trustProxy / BREWDOCS_TRUST_PROXY=1.

findings.title: Analytics/registry endpoints leak when keys exist but no admin token is set
findings.detail: needsAuth was driven by the token, so with keys present and BREWDOCS_TOKEN unset, /api/sites, /api/registry, /api/search and the /api/stats rollup answered unauthenticated. They now call authorizeRead and 401 unless the admin token or a valid key is presented; with no auth configured at all they stay open for the local drop-in UI.

findings.title: Theme slot partials resolved relative to the manifest (arbitrary file read)
findings.detail: A themes/brand.yml committed by a repo owner could name a slot value like ../../id_rsa; manifestSlots() read it and the build could embed it in a published page. Slot partials are now confined to the manifest's source root (recorded by loadThemeManifest as `sourceRoot`), boundary-aware in the same way as INV-5.

findings.title: Pages workflow uses npm install instead of npm ci
findings.detail: .github/workflows/brewdocs.yml ran `npm install` on a tree that contains package.json scripts, with pages: write + id-token: write granted. It now uses `npm ci`; the gate refuses any workflow that reintroduces `npm install`.

findings.title: Doc/reality drift (test counts, root package version, gitignored roadmap)
findings.detail: Test counts, file/LOC totals and the HTTP surface table are now parsed by scripts/map.mjs instead of typed, and CI fails when the map is stale. The root package.json version now tracks the three workspaces (4.1.0). ROADMAP.md remains gitignored by design (it is local planning, like AGENTS.md and the release notes).

findings.title: python adapter executes a bundled helper against the target tree
findings.detail: The python adapter executes a bundled AST helper against the tree. Sources fetched from npm/git are now flagged Source.fetched, propagated to AdapterContext, and the adapter refuses (warn + skip) rather than running against code the user did not choose locally.

findings.title: No CSRF/Origin check on write endpoints
findings.detail: Any web page could POST to an open instance on the user's LAN with a simple request (no preflight). POST endpoints now 403 when Origin does not match the Host, or Sec-Fetch-Site is not same-origin/none. Non-browser clients send neither header and are unaffected.

findings.title: No golden-output test for the renderer
findings.detail: The renderer emits its own CSS/JS and had no golden-output test, which is how the attribute-injection XSS (#3) survived 311 green tests. render.golden.test.ts now snapshots a full deterministic page with a hostile link/description, so an escaping regression fails loudly.

findings.title: api.test.ts was flaky under load (2 tests at a 30s timeout)
findings.detail: A full-suite run on 2026-09-26 failed two endpoint tests at 31.2s / 33.9s against `{ timeout: 30_000 }`; a solo run of the file passed in 28.7s and an immediate re-run of the full suite went green. Both tests do a full TS extraction synchronously, so they are sensitive to load. Found by running the suite while building the map generator.

findings.title: A fetched repo brewdocs.yml could name a plugin, executing arbitrary code at build time (RCE)
findings.detail: Reproduced by execution on 2026-09-28, not inferred: a synthetic repo whose brewdocs.yml contained plugins: [./pwn.cjs], with the plugin writing a marker file, ran that code during brewdocs build. loadPlugin resolves the specifier with requireFrom(root)(abs) — no signature, no sandbox — and build.ts called loadPlugins(config.plugins, ...) with no check of source.fetched. The guard for this class already existed and was simply not applied: finding #15 / INV-17 made the python adapter refuse a fetched source for exactly this reason. Three further bypasses were found while fixing it, all the same root cause (a Source rebuilt without carrying fetched): the per-version worktree in buildVersions, the extractVersion checkout, and the CLI build command resolveCliSource, which dropped the flag on the main brewdocs build path. All four sites now propagate fetched and resolveSetup drops repo-config plugins for a fetched source. Operator-passed --plugins still load, since that is the caller own choice, and a locally chosen source is unaffected.

findings.title: Credentials were compared with === (not constant-time)
findings.detail: requireSiteAccess compared the sha256 of a presented token with the stored tokenHash using === (server.ts), and the same shape appeared at every other credential site: the admin-token Bearer compares in authorize/authorizeRead, the site-org membership check in canAccessOrg, the API-key lookup in validateKey/revokeKey/claimSite, and the custom-domain verification token in verifyDomain. String comparison in JS is not guaranteed constant-time, so each byte leaks a little timing signal; with a high-entropy digest the practical exploitability is very low, which is why this is low severity, but the canonical hardening is cheap. All sites now route through one helper, safeEqual (core/src/compare.ts), which wraps crypto.timingSafeEqual. The wrapper exists because timingSafeEqual throws RangeError on a length mismatch — and a throw in this server exits the process (finding #21), so a naive swap would have traded a timing leak for an unauthenticated crash. safeEqual returns false instead, keeps === semantics (byte comparison, not digest comparison, so passing a pre-hashed value never silently becomes valid), and answers false for non-strings. Verified by execution, not inference: the scan that found these sites is now gate check inv-23, and the swap was proven by mutation (reverting any one site turns the gate red).

findings.title: One malformed request could kill the process (async handler throw)
findings.detail: Found while fixing #20: the swap to crypto.timingSafeEqual would have thrown RangeError on any wrong-length token, and that throw would have exited the server. Reproduced by execution: an async http request listener that throws rejects a promise with no handler attached, and Node exits the process (verified against the real server with a hostile request line, GET //[ — new URL() throws ERR_INVALID_URL before any route runs). Three distinct surfaces had the same defect class: buildRequestHandler (async, so any throw anywhere in any route kills the process), serveStatic in cli/src/index.ts (a synchronous listener, same outcome on a bad request line or a lone % in decodeURIComponent), and fs.createReadStream(...).pipe(res) on both static paths (a file removed between the existence check and the open emits unhandled error → process exit; verified with a stream to a missing file). Fixed with a single try/catch wrapper around the shared route body plus a 400 for the unparseable request line, a 400 in the preview server, and error handlers on both streams. A client that abandons a POST mid-body (the body read throws aborted) now yields a clean response instead of a crash. Verified by execution: hostile request lines, aborted bodies, and a wrong-length site token all leave the server answering 200 on the next request.

findings.title: A stored API-key hash authenticated as a credential (pass-the-hash)
findings.detail: Found while auditing the comparison sites for #20, and reproduced by execution over HTTP, not inferred: create an org, add a member with a raw bd_live_ key, read the member keyHash out of .cloud.json, then GET a private org site with Authorization: Bearer <that hash> — the server answered 200. Mechanism: canAccessOrg used normalizeKeyHash, which passes a non-bd_live_ string through untouched because that convenience exists for addOrgMember/removeOrgMember (an operator may paste either form). Authentication is different: the stored hash is an artifact at rest, and if presenting it back is sufficient then hashing buys nothing — anyone who can read .cloud.json (a backup, a synced folder, a hosting dir served or copied by mistake) holds every member credential in usable form. validateKey in cli/src/keys.ts never had this hole (it always hashes what it is presented, so the hash double-hashes and misses), which is why the asymmetry went unnoticed: the two key stores disagreed about what a credential is. Fixed by hashing in canAccessOrg (hashKey, not normalizeKeyHash), with the reason written at the call site. addOrgMember/removeOrgMember keep accepting a hash, because there the caller is the operator, not a request. Tests: packages/core/test/cloud.test.ts asserts the stored hash is rejected and the raw key still works.
